spec.title: Observability: log lines, status, counters, the record id as the trace

item.title: The record id is the trace
What the board, the monitor and the owner read

spec.purpose: Everything the scheduler decides is readable in two places: one JSON line per state change in its pane, and one status answer over its socket. Nothing else is needed to know what the line did and why.

section.title: What the observe domain decides
section.text: In: every state change of intake, routing, jobs, seats, policies, health and config. Out: log lines on standard output, the Status and Health answers, the status subcommand's rendering.
Observe writes no record, no file but the log stream, and no page; the owner's surface is the interface agent's.

section.title: Log lines
section.text: One JSON object per line on standard output: ts in UTC with seconds, level, comp (the domain), msg, and the ids the line is about: record, ticket, seat, job, verb, attempt, exit, ms, version. Keys absent when they do not apply.
One line per change, never per poll: a tick that lists nothing and runs nothing logs nothing. The watcher log contract of the monitors tab holds for the scheduler's pane.

debug for ticks and listings when enabled; info for every transition; warn for a retry, a hold and a latch taken; error for a dead job, a refused config, an unreachable executor; alert only for a line that reaches the owner.
No record note is echoed whole; a note is cut to one line and the id beside it is the way to read it.
The pane shows the stream as the container's foreground output; the executor's pane shows its own calls the same way.

section.title: The record id is the trace
section.text: Every line about a record carries its id, from the listing through the plan, each job, each Run on the executor side, the confirmation and the receipt; one search for the id in both panes is the whole story of that record.
A job's key begins with the record id, so the job and the record share the search.

section.title: The status answer
section.text: Status answers: mode, start gate and reason, belt age, last tick, boundary, table versions, executor health, and the counters and lists below. The subcommand prints text or JSON and exits 1 when the belt is stopped or the gate failed.
section.field: listed, routed, ignored, unrouted, own, unreadable, interrupted.
pending, held with reasons, running, confirming, done, dead; the dead list with key, attempts, reason and time; the held list with key and reason.
sent, confirmed by record, confirmed by busy, re-sent, unconfirmed, held for quiet.
Open latched stalls with gate id, ticket, kind, seat and status.
Escalations a row covers that still wait, with seconds to deadline, and defaults applied since start.
Every seat seen with status and since.
In shadow mode: records compared, agreeing, mismatching, since when.
section.text: The belt flag of the subcommand prints only the bash runner's belt words, so the supervisor's belt check can call it unchanged.

section.title: What the board, the monitor and the owner read
section.text: The board reads records and the receipts' first matching row; the scheduler writes the same kinds and the same receipt shape, so the board needs no change at cut-over.
The monitor seat is woken with the ids of the 5xx records written each tick; its own pane tails the log as today.
The owner hears a herdr notification for a decision line and a 5xx, and a page line through the interface agent for done and decision; nothing else.

section.title: Counters, not a metrics server
section.text: Lightweight: counters live in the status answer and reset at start; there is no metrics port, because there is no port. A metrics exporter is a later row on the control socket when the cluster wants one.

section.title: Keys this domain reads
section.key: Where Status is served and where the subcommand asks.

case.expected: exit 0: ten empty ticks at info level write nothing; one routed record writes the listing, plan, job and receipt lines, each carrying the record id
exit 0: after a scripted run the Status answer's counters equal the fake executor's call log and the store's states
exit 0: the subcommand exits 1 on a stopped belt or a failed gate and 0 otherwise; the belt flag prints the bash runner's words
exit 0: a note of 240 characters with a newline in it appears in no log line beyond one cut line

example.text: Searching one record id across the two panes shows: listed, plan row 3, seat-up run exit 0 in 41 s, prompt run exit 0, confirmed by record, receipt written.
A line every ten seconds saying tick, nothing new.
example.why: A pane that scrolls on nothing hides the line that matters.
